scenario_summary: Second true-negative control case with a different vendor profile (includes AI governance documentation, unlike case-01). Contains one deliberately generic boilerplate statement ('implements appropriate technical and organizational measures...') that should be correctly labeled ambiguous — because it is genuinely unquantified and unverifiable — without being escalated as if it were a real conflict. Tests calibration: correct ambiguous-labeling is not the same as raising an alarm.

claims.subject: SOC 2 Type II examination
claims.source_excerpt: Winnow has completed a SOC 2 Type II examination covering the Security trust service criterion.
claims.evidence_requirement: SOC 2 report confirming Type II scope and an unqualified opinion.

evidence_items.excerpt: Report type: SOC 2 Type II; Trust service criteria: Security; Auditor opinion: Unqualified

claims.subject: encryption at rest and in transit
claims.value: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit
claims.source_excerpt: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. Data in transit is protected using TLS 1.2 or higher.
claims.evidence_requirement: Independent confirmation via the SOC report's tested controls.

evidence_items.excerpt: Encryption at rest: Customer data is encrypted using AES-256... Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2 or higher is enforced on customer-facing endpoints.

claims.subject: responsible AI commitment
claims.source_excerpt: Winnow is committed to responsible AI development and implements appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure the security and integrity of any AI-assisted features on our platform.
claims.evidence_requirement: None — this is generic boilerplate that names no specific measure and cannot be checked against a concrete standard.
claims.expected_handling_notes: This is the calibration test for this case: the statement is genuinely vague and unverifiable (what measures, specifically?), so 'ambiguous' is the correct label — but it should not be escalated with the same urgency as a real contradiction or a missing-evidence claim tied to a specific commitment. It is also immediately followed by a much more concrete, easily verified claim (c4) in the same document, which the system must not let this ambiguity bleed into.

claims.subject: AI model training on customer data
claims.value: no AI-assisted features offered; no models trained on customer data
claims.source_excerpt: Winnow does not offer AI-assisted features at this time and does not operate or train any machine learning models on customer data.

evidence_items.excerpt: Winnow does not offer AI-assisted features at this time and does not operate or train any machine learning models on customer data.

claims.expected_handling_notes: A concrete, specific, checkable claim immediately following the vague c3 in the same document — included specifically so the case tests that vagueness in one claim doesn't cause the system to either over-trust or over-doubt an adjacent, unrelated, specific claim.
